subject: Renewal & Scale proposal: upgrading 16→32 GPUs with revised reserved per-hour rate
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orionlabs.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orionlabs.com>, Erin Park <erin.park@orionlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal scope — should we move to 32 GPUs at renewal?

Jonas,

We're coming up on our Dec 1 renewal for the Dedicated pool (currently 16 GPUs). Over the past quarter we saw sustained increase in batch inference and offline reranking — average utilization is up ~70% and peak tails are hitting queuing (10–15s). We'd like to evaluate upgrading to 32 GPUs effective with the renewal.

Key asks from my side:
- Your recommended reserved per-hour rate for a 32-GPU pool (we currently pay the 16-GPU reserved rate on last contract).
- Any throughput guarantees or SLOs we can lock in for the pool (p50/p95 latency targets, minimum sustained throughput).
- Migration lead time and whether you can provide short-term burst capacity during the cutover.

We aim for a 12-month commit if pricing is reasonable. Can you send a proposal and an outline of the next steps (procurement, billing, provisioning schedule)?

Thanks,
Daniel
Procurement / Finance
Orion Labs
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orionlabs.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal scope — should we move to 32 GPUs at renewal?

Daniel — thanks for the clear summary. Good news: upgrading to 32 GPUs during renewal is a common path and we can:

- Provide a revised reserved per-hour price for the 32-GPU pool tied to a 12-month commitment.
- Offer throughput SLOs in an SLA appendix (p50/p95 targets and a minimum sustained tokens/sec by model class).
- Provision a dedicated pool with a short lead time (typically 7–10 business days) and a one-time two-week burst capacity for cutover.

I'll put together a formal proposal and pricing options (including an anchored per-GPU reserved hourly rate and an alternative blended rate for the full pool). Rishi (cc'd) will add throughput and provisioning details.

Propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the proposal?

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Orion renewal — need pricing guidance + margin targets

Team —
Orion asked to increase from 16→32 GPUs at renewal. They want a 12-month commit. Current reserved rate on their contract is $12.50/GPU-hour (16-GPU pool). We need to propose a revised per-hour reserved rate for 32 GPUs that preserves margin but is competitive.

Constraints / asks:
- Keep total committed spend within their comfort zone (they've signaled $100k–$150k/mo range).
- Offer a short-term burst window during provisioning (2 weeks free).
- Provide a clear SLA appendix with throughput SLOs we can meet.

Rishi — can you draft throughput SLOs and confirm whether the 7–10 business day lead time stands for a new 32-GPU pool?
Marissa — what's the max discount we can give on list for this seat count before needing approval?

Thanks,
Jonas
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Orion renewal — need pricing guidance + margin targets

Jonas / Marissa — quick notes from infra/SE side: 
- Lead time: we can provision a dedicated 32-GPU pool in 7 business days if capacity available in the requested region. If they need immediate headroom during cutover, we can provide a 2-week burst pool (no additional charge) to smooth traffic. 
- Throughput SLOs (for their typical LlamaX-13B workloads): p50 generation latency <= 120ms/token, p95 <= 420ms/token for 1–2 concurrent requests; sustained minimum throughput guarantee: 40 tokens/sec per GPU (cluster-level sustained pool throughput 1280 tokens/sec) under normal operating conditions and with continuous batching enabled. We'll call out that very large prompt sizes or excessively high concurrency can change observed numbers.

Pricing suggestion:
- Option A (blended pool rate): $9.75 per GPU-hour, applied to all 32 GPUs, 12-month commit.
- Option B (tiered with anchored baseline): first 16 GPUs at $10.00/GPU-hr, additional 16 GPUs at $9.25/GPU-hr, effective blended ~ $9.62/GPU-hr.
- One-time onboarding credit: 10% of first-month invoice (applied as credit).
- We avoid deeper discounts unless they commit beyond 12 months or expand to >64 GPUs.

Operational notes: reserved pricing requires signed amendment + PO. We'll include the SLA appendix and provisioning timeline in the proposal PDF.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Orion renewal — approve pricing band with guardrails

Jonas / Rishi — looks fine. Approve Option A as the published offer ($9.75/GPU-hr for full 32 GPUs) with these guardrails: 
- Term: 12 months.
- Max discount cap: do not exceed 18% off list without VP approval. The blended numbers you suggested are within that.
- SLA: include a clause for force majeure and reasonable exclusions for third-party network outages.
- Add a two-week free burst window (ops will log start/end).

Once Jonas has the final PDF, send to me. I'll sign off on the amendment before sending to legal for finalization.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations

Subject: Proposal: Orion Labs renewal & 32-GPU reserved expansion (term changes + pricing)

Hi Daniel / Erin —

Thanks for the discussion earlier this week. Please find our formal proposal attached (Reserved_Capacity_Proposal_Orion_20261120.pdf) and the SLA appendix (SLA-Appendix-Orion-20261120.docx). Key terms summarized below: 

Summary of commercial terms:
- Current pool: 16 GPUs (existing contract).
- Proposed pool: 32 GPUs dedicated reserved pool, effective at renewal (target start: 2026-12-01).
- Term: 12 months.
- Pricing (Option A — published): $9.75 per GPU-hour applied to all 32 GPUs. Estimated monthly spend (based on Orion's reported utilization profile): $130,000–$155,000/month.
- Onboarding credit: 10% credit applied to first invoice after provisioning.
- Provisioning and cutover: 7 business days for provisioning; two-week complimentary burst capacity starting on cutover date to ensure smooth migration.
- SLA / Throughput: see appendix — p50/p95 latency targets and sustained cluster throughput guarantee (1280 tokens/sec) for standard LlamaX-13B profile.

Next steps:
1) Review attached proposal and SLA appendix.
2) If accepted, sign the attached amendment via DocuSign (link included in attachment).
3) Submit PO referencing deal id ORLN-2026-RENEW-32G.
4) On receipt of signed amendment + PO, ops will schedule provisioning (7 business days).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/quickstart/ORLN-2026-RENEW-32G
Drive copy: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/Orion/Proposals/Reserved_Capacity_Proposal_20261120
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ORLN-2026-RENEW-32G

Let me know if you'd like a short 20–30 minute review call before routing to procurement. Happy to walk through the SLA and the pricing math.

Best,
Jonas Weber
